evidence: The pre-fix code used identityOf({role:'assistant',content}) as the assistant_response identity and skipped the push when already seen, so two requests that both replied "OK" produced one entry and the second request vanished from the timeline; commit 5792d4d shows the identity became `asst:${record.requestId}` while the role+content hash is still unconditionally seeded into seenIdentities, which is exactly what the reviewer proposed.
guidance_note: When one computed identity answers two questions (per-request attribution and cross-request dedup), give each question its own field before writing the dedup loop.

evidence: memoKey was safeChain.map(r=>r.requestId).join('|') with deps [memoKey], so a record going streaming -> complete could not invalidate the memo and the tab kept the in-flight placeholder; 5792d4d rebuilt the key as `${requestId}:${state}:${hasResponse}` per record.
guidance_note: Build a memo key from every field the memoized function reads, not from the collection's shape.

evidence: BoundaryRow rendered a <button> whose handler was `onSelectRequest?.(entry.requestId)`, so with the optional prop absent the DOM carries a focusable control that does nothing; the fix introduced RequestIdLink which picks button-or-span from the prop's presence.
guidance_note: When a click-handler prop is optional, choose the element tag from the prop's presence at the moment the control is written, instead of relying on optional chaining in the handler.

evidence: EntryShell's attribution chip carried the identical optional-handler-button defect as BoundaryRow, so the reviewer had to raise the same issue twice in one round; one RequestIdLink helper fixed both.
guidance_note: After writing the first control that takes an optional handler, sweep the file for the other controls taking the same prop rather than shipping two copies of the pattern.

evidence: document.querySelector searches the whole document, so any other node carrying data-tool-use-id (a second detail pane, an un-cleaned test DOM) can win; only one ConversationTab mounts today so the misfire was latent rather than live, which makes the premise right in kind and overstated in urgency.
guidance_note: Scope a DOM lookup to the subtree that rendered the trigger (closest() on the container) the first time the query is written.

evidence: The request_boundary push appears as unchanged context in 5792d4d's patch, so its stopReason/durationNs semantics are original-PR code the flag caught only because the fix rewrote lines above it; the reviewer's claim is right - computeLatency uses endedNs ?? completedNs and ChainStopReasonStrip falls back to end_turn. The agent cited single-enforcer while explicitly declining to import computeLatency, i.e. it copied the rule into a second place under a law that forbids exactly that.
guidance_note: When a new surface renders a value another surface already derives (latency, stop reason), call the existing derivation instead of restating its rule.

evidence: fnv1a64Hex is untouched in 5792d4d's patch, so the limb implementation is original-PR code, not fix-caused; the reviewer's arithmetic claim is correct (the 2^8 term is counted both inside 0x1b3 and again via lo3/hi3) and the BigInt rewrite reproduces the published vectors cbf29ce484222325 / af63dc4c8601ec8c / 85944171f73967e8.
guidance_note: Never hand-roll a specified algorithm's arithmetic without pinning its published test vectors in the same commit; the optimization was written before any vector could contradict it.

evidence: 5792d4d rewrote the comment directly above memoKey but left the file-header [LAW:one-source-of-truth] block still claiming the key is the joined requestIds and that a completion 'flips the chain reference in Live.tsx' - the same invariant stated twice, one copy updated.
guidance_note: After changing an invariant, grep the file for every other place that states it; the fix updated the adjacent comment and missed the header restating the same claim.

evidence: 7df68a5 (the F7 fix) added the comment 'Reference test vectors (pinned in `fnv1a64Hex matches canonical FNV-1a-64 test vectors`)' in the same commit that added that test, and the test asserts only /^[0-9a-f]{16}$/ plus distinctness - the comment named a proof that did not exist.
guidance_note: When a comment names a test as the proof of a claim, write the assertion that proves it in the same commit.

evidence: The test added by 7df68a5 says 'We compute these once and pin them. Any change to stableJson OR fnv1a64Hex flips these values' but asserts only hex format and set-size 3, so it passes under a completely wrong hash function - the regression guard the F7 fix claimed to add was vacuous.
guidance_note: A regression test that asserts only shape and distinctness proves nothing; pin the literal expected output or do not claim the value is pinned.

evidence: d826973 touched only the contentHash/fnv1a export region and ConversationTab's header, not stableJson, so this is original-PR code re-surfaced in a later round; the claim is right - a function-valued property falls through to `return "null"` and serializes as "key":null while JSON.stringify omits the key.
guidance_note: When a serializer's comment claims parity with JSON.stringify, enumerate JSON.stringify's non-JSON cases (undefined/function/symbol, object position vs array position) before writing the loop.

evidence: The raw interpolation `[data-tool-result-id="${toolUseId}"]` is original-PR code (db40732 touched only stableJson and its tests), and an id containing `"]` makes querySelector throw a SyntaxError inside the click handler; the fix changed the prop from a prebuilt selector to {attr,value} so a caller cannot supply an unescaped selector at all.
guidance_note: Never interpolate an externally-supplied string into a selector; take the attribute and the raw value as separate parameters and escape inside the helper.

evidence: 8842449 changed only ConversationTab.tsx and its test, so the AssistantResponseEntry comment is original-PR text; it described a nullable content field that the declared type (`readonly content: AnthropicContentBlock[]` plus a boolean inFlight) never had.
guidance_note: When a field's shape changes during design, re-read the comment attached to it - the 'null while in-flight' text survived the switch to an always-array plus boolean discriminator.

evidence: d18f227 touched only the conversation.ts interface comment, so `status: partial.status ?? 200` is original-PR test-helper code; with RequestRecord.status typed number|null the helper silently rewrote an intentional null to 200, making a whole branch of the type untestable.
guidance_note: In a test factory over a type with nullable fields, default with `key in partial` rather than `??`, so null stays expressible.

evidence: Identical defect to F14 in the second copy of makeRequest in conversation.test.ts; the same `??` default had been duplicated into two test files, so one mistake produced two findings in one round.
guidance_note: Two test files sharing a record factory should share one factory module; duplicating it duplicated the nullable-field bug.

evidence: buildToolPairings keys both maps off tool_use_id (the tool_result branch reads rec.tool_use_id), so the name toolResultToUse misdescribed its key; the code is original-PR code untouched by d18f227. The cited law is about one type per behavior and the change was a rename to a symmetric naming convention.
guidance_note: Name a map after key-and-value ('<thing>IndexBy<key>') when it is created, not after the direction of the lookup you happen to be writing.

evidence: timelineRowKey returned `b:${requestId}-${index}` while boundaries are one-per-request, so the index added a second, drifting identity that forces unmount/remount when an earlier entry is inserted; original-PR code, not fix-caused.
guidance_note: Derive a React key from the entry's own unique field; append an array index only when the entry has no identity of its own.

evidence: The BigInt rewrite in 7df68a5 (the F7 fix) iterates str.charCodeAt(i) while the comment it added asserts 'The 16-char hex result is canonical FNV-1a output' - the fix introduced the canonicality claim and covered only its ASCII half; the agent then switched to TextEncoder bytes, and the pinned ASCII vectors still hold because ASCII UTF-8 equals its code units. The single-enforcer citation is for reusing one module-scope TextEncoder instance, which is instance reuse, not rule enforcement.
guidance_note: When rewriting a hash to be canonical, settle the input encoding at the same moment as the constants - canonical FNV-1a is defined over bytes, not UTF-16 code units.

evidence: Both cssEscape and the comment claiming its minimal escape 'is sufficient for the values in a [attr="..."] selector' were added by the F12 fix in 8842449; a raw newline or NUL is invalid inside a CSS string, so the sufficiency claim was false as written even though the try/catch keeps it harmless.
guidance_note: Describe a fallback you cannot exercise by what it covers and what backstops it, rather than asserting it sufficient.

narrative: Nine rounds on one 2071-line feature PR, and the reviewer surfaced only a handful of original-code issues per round, so most rounds were the review tool draining its own backlog rather than the agent's fixes failing. Five findings were genuinely fix-caused and all five are documentation: a memo-key invariant restated in a file header that the fix did not update (F8), and three findings chasing a hash rewrite whose new comment claimed canonical output and named a test that asserted nothing (F9, F10, F18). The agent accepted all nineteen findings; every acceptance was the right call, and two of the reviewer's catches (the identical-content dedup collapse in F1 and the FNV prime bug in F7) were real defects that would have shipped. The recurring self-inflicted cost is comment-versus-code drift: the agent writes dense law-annotated prose blocks that then need maintaining, and each fix's new prose became the next round's finding.
guidance_observations: Every fix-caused finding in this PR was a comment or a test comment, never broken behavior - the drift cost two of nine rounds.
The agent's habit of restating an invariant in both a file header and an inline comment guarantees that half of it goes stale on the next change.
Law tokens were sometimes attached to changes that contradict them: F6 cites single-enforcer while deliberately duplicating computeLatency's rule instead of importing it.
The first fix commit (5792d4d) rewrote the comment next to the code it changed but not the header saying the same thing, which is the single cheapest round to have avoided.

evidence: The PR converted a <span> hash badge into a <button> with no type attribute, and HTML's default is type=submit; commit 0be3ed6 adds type="button" to that badge and to the sibling filter button.
guidance_note: When promoting a static element to a <button>, write type="button" in the same edit rather than relying on the absence of an enclosing form.

evidence: 0be3ed6 (the F1 fix) added only type="button" to two buttons, so the badge whose accessible name is just the hash string is original-PR code; the reviewer is right that a toggle named '#abc123' announces no action and that title is not reliably announced.
guidance_note: When turning a label into a toggle, give it an action-oriented accessible name and aria-controls in the same edit that adds aria-expanded.

evidence: fullPromptText delegated to systemToText, which trimmed the string form and each array block, so the 'full' view could not reproduce the captured prompt; the function is original-PR code (0be3ed6 touched only PromptsPanel.tsx). The agent took the reviewer's second offered option and parameterized trimming.
guidance_note: When adding a 'full'/'raw' variant beside a 'preview' helper, parameterize the normalization instead of reusing the preview's normalizer and renaming the result.

evidence: Commit 1959529 (the F3 fix) wrote the new doc 'Returns the prompt text exactly as it was captured - no trimming, no normalization ... the literal bytes that were sent' onto a function that still drops non-text blocks and inserts synthetic "\n" separators for array-form system prompts.
guidance_note: Describe a rendering helper against every input shape it accepts (string and array) before claiming fidelity; the fix reasoned only about the string path it had just changed.

evidence: Commit 1e09ab3 (the F4 fix) reworded the doc to 'the text fields of each text-typed block ... non-text blocks are dropped' while the predicate still accepted any object with a string text field, so {type:"image",text:"GHOST"} would have been concatenated into the prompt; the fix added block.type === "text". The law citation labels a runtime discriminator check as a type-level guarantee.
guidance_note: When a doc rewrite names a discriminator ('text-typed'), make the predicate test that discriminator in the same commit instead of describing behavior the code does not have.

narrative: A 177-line follow-up PR that took five review rounds, three of them spent on the doc comment of one four-line helper. F3 flagged that fullPromptText trimmed; the fix's replacement comment overclaimed byte fidelity, which became F4; F4's replacement comment claimed the code filtered text-typed blocks, which it did not, which became F5. Every finding was correct and every acceptance was right, but rounds 2 and 3 exist purely because each fix's new prose asserted more than the code did. The single behavioral bug found in the whole PR (the loose block predicate) was found only because a comment claimed otherwise.
guidance_observations: The rewrite-the-comment fix is the highest-yield source of extra rounds here: two of five rounds came from prose written during review, not from the original PR.
A comment that describes what a function does should be checked against each input shape the function accepts, since the reviewer checks it that way.
The agent's fixes repeatedly widened a claim ('exactly as captured', 'literal bytes') beyond what it had verified; narrower prose would have ended the PR two rounds earlier.

evidence: filters.ts declares `export type ModelValue = string` (read at ref 2dcb35c), so toggleFilter("models", "large") compiles fine and the comment's claimed compile error was false; the agent agreed and rescoped the claim to the closed-enum categories in de003f0.
guidance_note: Do not write a comment asserting a compile error you have not tried to compile; check the alias behind the generic before documenting the guarantee.

evidence: passesFilters called all five extractors eagerly, including sizeBucketOf's JSON.stringify, for every record on every render; 1378116 changed matches(set, record, extract) to check set.size before invoking the extractor, which is the reviewer's own second suggestion.
guidance_note: In a per-record predicate, pass an expensive extractor as a function so the cheap constraint check gates it, rather than evaluating all inputs before composing.

evidence: The dropdown was role="listbox" containing <button role="option"> with no aria-multiselectable, which is an invalid listbox; 4665233 switched the whole control to menu / menuitemcheckbox, one of the reviewer's two offered options and the one matching independent toggles.
guidance_note: Choose the ARIA pattern from the interaction (independently togglable values means menuitemcheckbox) before writing roles onto an existing div/button tree.

evidence: The same false 'passing "large" to the models chip is a compile error' claim was written into FilterChips.tsx's header as well as proxy.ts's, and de003f0 had to correct both; one wrong belief produced two findings in the same round.
guidance_note: State a type-safety invariant in the one file that owns it; restating it in a consumer's header duplicated the error into a second place.

evidence: 1378116 (the F2 fix) rewrote matches()/passesFilters into a lazy AND chain but left the filters.ts header asserting 'the composer is .every() over the categories' and 'Each extractor runs unconditionally against every record' - the header described precisely the behavior the fix had just removed.
guidance_note: A module header that describes the algorithm must be edited in the same commit that changes the algorithm; the fix edited the function and skipped the file's own description of it.

evidence: 4665233 (the F3 fix) changed only role and aria-haspopup strings; `aria-expanded={isOpen}` and the `{isOpen && !disabled && ...}` gate are unchanged original-PR lines that the re-review surfaced, so the flag is a false positive. The reviewer's state is genuinely reachable: an open Model chip whose records drain renders aria-expanded=true with no popup and cannot be clicked shut. The agent cited types-are-the-program for a useEffect reconciliation that does not make the state unrepresentable, which is exactly what F14 later found.
guidance_note: When a control's render gate carries more conditions than its aria attribute, derive both from one expression where the gate is written.

evidence: SIZE_MEDIUM_BYTES/SIZE_LARGE_BYTES compared against JSON.stringify(body).length is original-PR code visible unchanged in the round-0 hunk, and b54a555 did not touch sizeBucketOf; the reviewer is right that .length counts UTF-16 code units, and the agent renamed the constants to *_CHARS, the first of the two offered options.
guidance_note: Name a threshold constant after the unit the expression actually produces; 'bytes' was wrong the moment the measure became a string length.

evidence: data-testid built from `label.toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g,"-")` is original-PR code untouched by b54a555; the FilterKey was already available as a stable id, so tying selectors to display copy was gratuitous coupling.
guidance_note: Derive test ids from the stable key that already identifies the thing, never from user-facing copy.

evidence: The option test id interpolated the raw option value, which for models is an open-set string from the wire; real Anthropic model ids contain no selector metacharacters, so the risk is latent rather than live, but the shape is genuinely unsafe. Original-PR code, untouched by b54a555.
guidance_note: Build a test id from a sanitized derivation of the identifier when the identifier is open-set, at the point the id is first written.

evidence: `disabled={!hasModelOptions}` with an observation-only option list is original-PR code; with a model selected and the record set drained the chip disabled itself while its selections stayed active, leaving no way to deselect except global Clear. The fix computed the option list as observed union selected, which removes the state rather than special-casing it.
guidance_note: The actionable option list of a filter control is observed-union-selected; compute it that way when the control is written, so draining the data cannot strand a selection.

evidence: The EXTRACTORS header claiming 'The chip UI reads from the same table to populate its dropdown options' is original-PR text present unchanged in the round-0 hunk; FilterChips never imports EXTRACTORS and uses static arrays plus observedModels.
guidance_note: A comment that names a second consumer is checkable - check the consumer's imports before writing the claim.

evidence: 7bc5232 (the F9 fix) introduced slugify(), which strips everything outside [a-z0-9] and therefore maps foo-bar and foo_bar to the same id: the fix made the ids selector-safe and simultaneously made them non-unique, which is the exact remainder the reviewer raised.
guidance_note: A sanitizer that maps many inputs onto one output needs a disambiguating suffix decided when the slug is written, not after a reviewer names a collision.

evidence: The call-count test that reassigns global JSON.stringify and restores it in a finally was added by 1378116, the F2 fix; the finding is about that newly added test's technique, not about the fix being wrong, and vi.spyOn was already available in this suite.
guidance_note: When a performance fix needs a call-count assertion, reach for the framework's spy rather than reassigning a global builtin.

evidence: b54a555 (the F6 fix) reconciled openKey inside a useEffect, so on the commit where modelOptions empties the button still renders aria-expanded=true with the popup suppressed - the same inconsistency F6 reported, one frame narrower; 5466bc9 replaced it with a render-time `const expanded = isOpen && !disabled` feeding both the attribute and the gate.
guidance_note: Fix a 'two things must agree' bug by deriving both from one expression, not by reconciling one to the other in an effect that runs after the render that can be observed.

evidence: 2dcb35c shows `const observed = observedModels(records)` was already unmemoized before the F10 fix, which added only the small mergeModelOptions pass over the model list on top of it, so the per-render full-capture scan the reviewer objects to is original-PR code rather than fix-caused.
guidance_note: Memoize a derivation that walks the full record set the moment it is placed in a component that re-renders on local UI state such as an open dropdown.

narrative: Seven rounds, fifteen findings, and eleven of them were original-PR issues that the reviewer simply had not surfaced yet - two rounds' worth of findings (F7 through F11) were entirely untouched original code. Four findings were genuinely fix-caused, and they split cleanly: F5 and F13 are the debris of the lazy-extractor fix (a stale module header and a monkeypatched builtin in the new test), while F12 and F14 are incomplete fixes that solved half of the problem they named - a slug that is selector-safe but not injective, and a reconciliation effect that narrows an inconsistent ARIA state instead of removing it. F14 is the sharpest lesson in the batch: the F6 reply cited [LAW:types-are-the-program] and claimed the bad state was 'unrepresentable past one render tick', and the next round found it inside that tick. Every acceptance was the right call and the agent never pushed back, including on F1/F4 where its own comment had asserted a compile error that does not exist.
guidance_observations: Two rounds were bought by half-fixes (slug without uniqueness, effect instead of derivation) that the agent's own reply described as making the bad state unrepresentable when it did not.
The phrase 'unrepresentable' in a fix reply should mean the state cannot be constructed, not that it is corrected one tick later; here that gap was worth a full round.
A fix that adds a new test can itself draw findings - the JSON.stringify monkeypatch arrived with a fix and cost a round.
The same false type-safety claim was written into two files, so one wrong belief produced two round-0 findings.

evidence: The module-scope paneDecoders map was cleared only on unsubscribe, and tmux reuses numeric pane ids across server restarts, so a buffered partial UTF-8 tail could prepend to the first chunk of a fresh stream; 296b99a moved the map into the onOutput closure and cleared it on every transition out of ready.
guidance_note: A per-key streaming-decoder map needs its invalidation boundary named where it is created; the connection lifetime, not process lifetime, owns per-pane decode state.

evidence: The charCodeAt&0xff loop is original-PR code from f0ca35b, not fix-caused, and it was correct: Buffer.from(text,'latin1') truncates code units above 0xFF the same way, so this round bought readability and a small speedup rather than fixing a defect. The cited law does not apply - there was one implementation, not a divergent second copy.
guidance_note: Use the platform's named encoding conversion (Buffer.from(s,'latin1')) when inverting a known transport encoding, instead of hand-rolling the byte loop.

evidence: F1's finding named both unbounded growth and reconnect contamination; the fix addressed the contamination and the reply explicitly accepted the leak ('Steady-state leak within one continuous session ... accepted'), so this is the deferred half coming back. No reply was possible in-PR: the PR merged at 2026-05-26T11:03:40Z and this review posted at 11:08:34Z.
guidance_note: When you consciously defer half of a finding, file the follow-up in the same reply so the deferral has a reference the next round can be pointed at.

evidence: The unit tests in output-router.test.ts are original-PR assertions over single ASCII chunks (verified in f0ca35b) and c17bebf touched only output-router.ts, so this is an original coverage gap, not fix-caused; the reviewer is right that the cross-chunk multi-byte split is the exact regression this PR exists to prevent and only the integration test exercises it. The review arrived five minutes after merge.
guidance_note: The regression a PR exists to prevent gets a unit test in that PR; an integration test that happens to cover it is not the guard.

evidence: The scrollback assertion is the original commit's ASCII "line1\nline2\nline3" case, so the missing non-ASCII coverage predates the review and is not fix-caused; it does mean the F2 implementation swap from a manual loop to Buffer.from went in with no test that could distinguish a wrong swap. Review posted after the merge.
guidance_note: When a review makes you swap one encoding implementation for another, add the assertion that distinguishes the two before pushing the swap.

evidence: joinChunks was added by the original commit f0ca35b and untouched by c17bebf, so the flag is a false positive; the O(n^2) characterization is technically accurate but the polling predicate runs over a handful of small chunks in one integration test, so the flakiness claim is speculative and the suggested incremental decoder would complicate the very concatenation the helper exists to demonstrate.

narrative: A small, well-aimed bug fix that took three rounds, none of which were caused by a bad fix. Round 1 raised an original-code style point (a hand-rolled latin1 byte loop) and round 2's four findings landed at 11:08:34Z, five minutes after the PR merged at 11:03:40Z, which is why all four sit unanswered and unresolved. Only F3 is fix-related, and only as the deferred half of F1 that the agent had explicitly reasoned about and accepted in writing. The real gap the post-merge round exposes is test coverage: the PR's entire thesis is cross-chunk multi-byte UTF-8 integrity, and the unit tests assert only single-chunk ASCII.
guidance_observations: Four findings were merged past because the review posted after the merge; nothing in the workflow reconciled them afterwards and the threads are still open.
The agent wrote a long law-annotated comment block justifying an accepted tradeoff, and the next reviewer raised that exact tradeoff anyway - prose in the code does not stop the finding.
Two of the post-merge findings ask for the test that the PR's own premise implies; adding the cross-chunk and non-ASCII cases with the fix would have pre-empted them.
